correctness.rationale: The explicit fourteen-facet complex is checked to be a connected orientable closed two-manifold with seven vertices, twenty-one edges, fourteen triangular faces, and Euler characteristic zero, hence a torus. The seven-vertex torus triangulation is unique up to isomorphism, so its face-incidence code is equivalent to the source example. The resulting generator has rank seven and minimum distance thirteen, matching the published parameters. Every one of the \(29211\) positive-dimensional message subspaces is enumerated uniquely in RREF, and the support of each generated subcode is exactly the union of its basis-word supports. Thus the histograms and hierarchy are exhaustive finite results.

value.rationale: The primary paper introduces arbitrary topological triangulations as a new geometric source of codes and highlights the seven-vertex torus as a canonical example. Generalized Hamming weights are the standard higher-dimensional refinement of minimum distance, and the complete support distribution records substantially more incidence information. Because the torus triangulation is the unique minimal genus-one example, its exact hierarchy and all subcode multiplicities form a natural reproducible higher-support fingerprint rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
